text: The maturity horizon is estimated with the same bias it is meant to remove. H is the p90 of root-to-close durations over CLOSED in-window lineages only (durs, line 437). (a) Right-censoring moves into the estimator: long lineages rooted near the cut are still open, so they are absent from durs and H comes out low. That is r10-02's 'keeps the short, drops the long' mechanism, now applied to the horizon. (b) A lineage that SHIPs at round 1 closes at its root review's own stamp (closure() returns ts_of(last) == root_ts), so its duration is exactly 0. Those zeros are the outcome being measured, and they push the p90 down. Verified: _p90([0]*9+[3d]) == 0. With H == 0, which is not None, every in-window lineage counts, including ones rooted seconds before the cut, and open lineages count as lower bounds. That is the original truncation, made worse. Trial lineages are the newest, so they sit nearest any too-short horizon and still show fewer fix rounds. H is also pooled over the outcome distribution, so it shifts between runs and when trial lineages close faster. The README says the cut is 'never on the outcome', but H is computed from outcomes. proposal: Fixed follow-up per lineage. Choose a constant F (e.g. 7 days, a named constant or --follow-up flag). A lineage counts when its root is stamped and root_ts <= cut − F. Its fix rounds and credit-outs are only those of reviews stamped within root_ts + F. Every lineage in every bucket then gets the same exposure, and the count does not depend on closure or on any statistic of the outcome. The metric becomes 'fix rounds within F'. A lineage longer than F is capped equally on both sides, and F can be chosen well past typical loop length.
